slides.say: In the figure, each vertex of rectangle A B C D is the center of a circle with a radius of two centimeters. Point O is the center of a circle that is tangent to the four quarter circles, and to sides A D and B C. What is the area of rectangle A B C D, in square centimeters?
The area of a rectangle is length times width. The short side, A B, is four, and it's written in the figure. So we need the long side, A D.
Along A D, the first part is a radius of the quarter circle at A, so it's two. The last part is a radius of the quarter circle at D, so it's also two.
at: the first part is a radius

slides.say: We'll solve it in two different ways. Let's start with estimation. To calculate that middle part exactly, we'd need a helper line and Pythagoras. But what if we don't see the helper line? Then we estimate the middle part from the figure.

slides: But wait. On the exam, a figure is not necessarily drawn to scale. So how can we estimate from the figure?

slides.say: In most cases, we can tell. First, most figures on the exam are accurate. Second, a rule of thumb. Regular shapes are drawn accurately: a square, a circle, an equilateral triangle, a cube.
at: most figures on the exam are accurate

slides: Why? A regular shape can't be drawn any other way. Here we have circles, and the middle circle touches all four quarter circles. If we make the figure bigger or smaller, the ratios between the parts stay the same. So here we can estimate from the figure.

slides.say: Look at the middle part. It's longer than a radius of the corner circles, and that radius is two.
And it's shorter than the diameter of the middle circle. That diameter goes from the top side to the bottom side, so it's four.

slides: Can't tell by eye? Use your eraser. Mark the length of the middle part on its edge. Then hold it against a radius, and against the diameter.

slides.say: So the middle part is more than two and less than four. A D is made of three parts: two, the middle part, and two. Two plus two plus two is six, and two plus four plus two is eight. So A D is between six and eight.
at: So the middle part is more than two
A D is made of three parts
So A D is between six and eight

slides.say: The area is four times A D. Four times six is twenty-four, and four times eight is thirty-two. So the area is between twenty-four and thirty-two, and it isn't equal to either one.
[pause] Now the choices. Choice number four, forty, is more than thirty-two. It's out.
Choice number three, thirty-two. The middle part is less than four, so the area is less than thirty-two. It's out too.

Choice number two, sixteen root two. The area has to be more than twenty-four. Sixteen times one and a half is sixteen plus eight, twenty-four. So to pass twenty-four, the root has to be more than one and a half.
at: Sixteen times one and a half

slides.say: But one and a half squared is two and a quarter, which is more than two. So root two is less than one and a half, and sixteen root two is less than twenty-four. It's out.
at: But one and a half squared
sixteen root two is less than twenty-four

slides.say: Three choices are out, so choice number one, sixteen root three, is our answer.

[pause] Now the math way. The estimate came from the figure. The math way uses only the given lengths, so it proves the answer. The middle circle touches the top and bottom sides, four apart. Its diameter is four, so its radius is two. Draw a line from A to O, joining two touching circles' centers.

The corner circle has radius two, and the middle circle has radius two. The circles touch from the outside, so A O is two plus two, four. From O, draw a perpendicular to side A B. Call its foot H. O is two below the top side, so A H is two. Now A H O is a right triangle, with hypotenuse four and one leg two.
at: A O is two plus two, four
hypotenuse four and one leg two

slides.say: Call O H x. By Pythagoras, x squared plus two squared is four squared. Four squared is sixteen, and two squared is four. Subtract four, and x squared is twelve.

The same construction on the right has the same hypotenuse, four, and the same vertical leg, two. So its horizontal length is also x. The whole rectangle is x plus x across. That's why A D is two x, not just x.
Now x itself. x squared is twelve, so x is the root of twelve. Twelve is four times three. So the root of twelve is the root of four, times the root of three. That's two root three.
at: so x is the root of twelve

slides.say: A D is two x, so it's four root three. The other side is four. Four times four root three is sixteen root three. That's choice number one, just like the estimate. Choice number one is our answer, and I'll see you in the next question.
at: Choice number one is our answer
